references.text: Isaiah predicts that the Redeemer will be 'highly exalted' (Hebrew: *nissah*), a concept directly linked in John 8:28 to crucifixion ('lifted up') as proof of Jesus' divine identity.
God commands Israel to know that 'I AM' (*Ehyeh*), a title Jesus uses in John 8:28 ('that I am') to confirm his identity as the true God and the one who speaks only the Father's words.
Here the Messiah expresses that he does not act on his own, but that the Lord God has sent him, a theme repeated in John 8:28 where Jesus says he does nothing of himself.
The suffering servant listens to the Father and speaks only what he is taught, paralleling Jesus' statement in John 8:28 that he speaks as the Father has taught him.
Jesus draws a direct parallel between Moses lifting up the serpent in the wilderness and his own exaltation, which is the context for the claim in John 8:28 that exaltation leads to recognition.
